q: AI 编码面试相对传统算法面试，最明显的变化是什么？
q_en: What is the biggest shift from a traditional algorithm interview to an AI coding interview?
options: 只考察你记住多少提示词模板
只考系统设计画图，不写代码
从单函数白板题变成带AI的多文件代码库任务
完全不需要写代码，AI 全包办
options_en: It only tests how many prompt templates you memorized.
It only tests system-design diagrams, no coding at all.
It shifts from a single-function whiteboard question to a multi-file codebase task with AI.
It means you never write code yourself because AI does everything.
why: 候选人常面对多文件代码库，需要修 bug、加功能、处理扩展，而不是只写三十到五十行的算法函数。
why_en: AI coding interviews swap a single-function whiteboard problem for a multi-file real-codebase task with an AI assistant.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Traditional[Write all code] --> AIInterview[Direct AI plus code]
  AIInterview --> Judge[Judgment visible]
  AIInterview --> Verify[Verification visible]

termDefinitions.meaning: 人工智能，这里specifically指面试里帮你生成/修改代码的编程助手模型（类似 Copilot）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AI here means the coding-assistant model that generates or edits code for you during the interview.

optionExplanations: 评分从来不是看你背了多少提示词，这个说法把考察重点想窄了。
这类面试仍然要写代码调代码，不是只画架构图。
对，题目规模和产出量真的从单函数跳到了多文件代码库。
AI 再快也不会替你写完全部代码，你还是要动手改。
optionExplanations_en: Scoring was never about how many prompt templates you memorized.
You still write and debug real code here, not just draw diagrams.
Right — the scope really does jump from one function to a codebase spanning multiple files.
AI speeds things up, but it doesn't finish all the code for you.
scenario: 你准备一场 60 分钟的 AI 编码面试，题目是在已有的多文件仓库里加功能并修 bug。
scenario_en: You're prepping for a 60-minute AI coding interview where you add a feature and fix bugs in an existing multi-file repo.

scenario: 传统编码面试通常只要写三十到五十行单函数代码；AI 编码面试里，AI 几秒内就能吐出跨多个文件、合计数百行的改动。
scenario_en: A traditional coding interview may ask for 30 to 50 lines in one function; with AI, you may get hundreds of lines across files in seconds.
q: 这个数量级差距，对你安排验证节奏有什么直接要求？
q_en: What does this scale difference require from your verification rhythm?
options: 必须按模块、每次生成后就验证，不能留到最后一次性通读
可以完全跳过阅读，因为 AI 已经保证正确
只需要在面试最后五分钟通读一次即可
代码量变大后可以直接让面试官帮你检查
options_en: You must verify module by module after each generation, not read it all at once at the end.
You can skip reading entirely because AI already guarantees correctness.
You only need one read-through in the last five minutes.
Once the code grows large you can just ask the interviewer to check it for you.
why: 代码量从几十行变成几百行跨文件，面试尾声一次性通读的时间成本会超过剩余时间；只有按模块分次验证，才能跟上 AI 的生成速度，这个节奏后续直接决定你还剩多少时间修复问题。
why_en: AI can produce hundreds of lines across files in seconds, so you must verify module by module as you go instead of reading it all at once at the end.
optionExplanations: 对，跟上 AI 的生成速度只能靠边生成边按模块核对，不能攒到最后。
AI 生成的代码照样会有边界错误，跳过阅读等于把风险留到最后才爆。
几百行代码留到最后五分钟通读，根本读不完也来不及改。
面试官在评估你的判断，不是替你查错，这一步不能外包。
optionExplanations_en: Right — matching AI's output speed means checking each module right after it lands, not saving it all for later.
AI code can still have edge-case bugs; skipping the read just saves the risk for later.
A single pass in the last five minutes can't cover everything the AI wrote, let alone let you fix it.
The interviewer is evaluating your judgment, not doing your review for you.

scenario: AI 能在几秒内生成整段实现，但生成的逻辑往往嵌在你从没见过的代码风格里。
scenario_en: AI can generate a whole implementation in seconds, but the logic may sit inside a code style you have never seen before.
q: AI 编码面试里，哪项能力相对传统算法背诵变得更重要？
q_en: In an AI coding interview, which skill becomes more important than rote algorithm memorization?
options: 快速阅读陌生代码并理解上下文
背更多排序/图算法模板
只记住几句提示词开场白
尽量少和面试官说话
options_en: Quickly reading unfamiliar code and understanding its context.
Memorizing more sorting and graph algorithm templates.
Memorizing a few prompt opening lines.
Talking to the interviewer as little as possible.
why: AI 能生成大量代码，但不会替你读懂已有系统或它自己生成的结果；能不能快速定位上下文，直接决定你能不能做出正确判断。
why_en: Reading unfamiliar code quickly now matters more because AI can generate code but cannot own the context or judgment for you.
tradeoff: 快速读懂陌生代码上下文 vs 背诵排序/图算法模板
optionExplanations: 对，AI 吐代码快，但读懂陌生上下文、判断它接不接得上系统还得靠你自己。
算法模板在传统白板题里管用，但这类面试的瓶颈已经挪到读代码上，模板背再多也用不上。
提示词只是开口的钥匙，读不懂 AI 给的代码，提示词再顺也没用。
沟通是四个评估维度之一，少说话只会让面试官看不到你的判断过程，不是加分项。
optionExplanations_en: Right — AI can churn out code fast, but making sense of code you've never seen is still your job.
Algorithm templates matter in classic whiteboard rounds, but the bottleneck here has shifted to reading code, so templates alone don't help.
A prompt opener just gets the AI talking; it doesn't help you understand what comes back.
Communication is one of the four evaluated areas, so staying quiet only hides your judgment from the interviewer.

q: 很多候选人低估了 AI 编码面试中的哪种不自然感？
q_en: What unnatural part of AI coding interviews do many candidates underestimate?
options: 面试全程不能使用键盘打字
必须全程手写汇编代码
同时和 AI 以及面试官沟通
整场面试都不能运行任何代码
options_en: Not being allowed to type on a keyboard for the whole interview.
Having to hand-write assembly code the whole time.
Communicating with both the AI and the interviewer at the same time.
Not being allowed to run any code for the entire session.
why: 双线沟通会拉扯注意力，候选人容易只盯着 AI 输出而忘了让面试官同步跟上你的思路。
why_en: Candidates often underestimate how unnatural it feels to run two conversations at once, one with the AI and one with the interviewer.
optionExplanations: 键盘照常用，这个限制是编出来的，从没出现过。
从来没有要求手写汇编，这是无中生有的限制。
对，同时要跟 AI 对话又要让面试官跟上你，这种双线切换才是真正的不适感来源。
运行代码是验证的常规动作，这条限制并不存在。
optionExplanations_en: You use the keyboard normally — this restriction was made up.
Nobody asks you to hand-write assembly; that requirement doesn't exist here.
Right — keeping the AI thread and your interviewer thread running together is the real discomfort.
Running code is a normal verification step; this restriction isn't real.
scenario: 面试全程共享屏幕：你一边给 AI 写提示，一边要让面试官实时跟上你的思路。
scenario_en: You share your screen the whole interview, prompting the AI while keeping the interviewer following your reasoning live.

q: 补全两类常见形式：
q_en: Fill in the two common interview formats:
text: {{结构化}}面试提供浏览器环境、固定 AI 和阶段题；{{开放式}}面试使用自己的编辑器、AI 工具并共享屏幕。
why: 两类形式共享核心能力，但具体准备和战术差异很大：结构化重在阶段推进节奏，开放式重在工具自理和范围自定。
why_en: Structured and open-ended interviews share the same core skills but require different tactics because the environment and scope differ.

scenario: 你把原始题目粘给 AI，几秒内收到两百行看起来完整的代码。
scenario_en: You paste the raw prompt into AI and receive 200 lines of complete-looking code within seconds.
q: AI 为什么会让候选人"感觉很高产但其实在出问题"？
q_en: Why can AI make a candidate feel productive while the interview is actually going off track?
options: 它会自动让面试官满意，完全不需要你做任何介入
它只能输出一眼就能看穿的明显错误代码，不会伪装
完整输出制造进展感，掩盖了没计划没验证的事实
它会彻底阻止你自己动手写下任何一行代码逻辑
options_en: It automatically satisfies the interviewer without you needing to do anything at all.
It only produces obviously broken code that anyone can spot at a glance, never disguised.
The complete-looking output creates a sense of progress that hides the fact you never planned or verified it.
It completely stops you from writing even a single line of code logic yourself.
why: 两百行看起来完整的代码会制造进展感，但如果你没掌控方向、也说不清逻辑，面试官看到的是失控而不是产出。
why_en: AI creates a false sense of productivity because complete-looking code hides the absence of a plan, review, or ability to explain it.
optionExplanations: 面试官只根据你展示出来的判断打分，AI 不会替你讨好任何人。
AI 出的错往往看起来完全正常，不是一眼假，这正是危险所在。
对，两百行看着很像进度，其实掩盖了没计划没验证的事实。
AI 是加速你写代码，不是拦着你不让你动手。
optionExplanations_en: The interviewer scores the judgment you actually show; AI can't win them over for you.
AI mistakes often look perfectly normal, not obviously wrong — that's exactly the danger.
Right — 200 lines that look finished feel like progress, but they hide the fact you never planned or reviewed any of it.
AI speeds up your coding, it doesn't lock you out of writing any of it.

scenario: 你花时间打磨了一段很长很讲究措辞的提示词，AI 也顺利吐出了代码。
scenario_en: You spend time polishing a long, carefully worded prompt, and the AI successfully returns code.
q: 面试官如何看待"提示词写得花不花哨"这件事？
q_en: How do interviewers think about whether your prompt wording is fancy?
options: 面试官打分只看你的提示词写得够不够长
面试官打分只看你的提示里用没用英文
面试官从头到尾都不会看你怎么用 AI
不主要评分花哨提示，而是看你是否还在掌控方向
options_en: They mainly judge whether the prompt is long enough.
They mainly judge whether the prompt is written in English.
They never look at how you use AI, from start to finish.
They don't mainly score clever prompt wording, they watch whether you stay in control.
why: 提示词只是执行工具，真正被评估的是你有没有还在做问题拆解、判断和验证，而不是提示写得多讲究。
why_en: Interviewers care less about clever prompt wording and more about whether you remain in control of the work.
tradeoff: 提示词写得花哨 vs 持续掌控问题拆解与验证
optionExplanations: 提示词长度从不是评分依据，写得长不代表判断力强。
语言选择跟你的工程判断没关系，这不是评分点。
面试官其实全程都在盯着你和 AI 的互动，这个假设是错的。
对，真正被打分的是你有没有还在拆解问题、验证结果，提示词只是执行的工具。
optionExplanations_en: Prompt length was never the scoring basis; a longer prompt doesn't prove better judgment.
Which language you prompt in has nothing to do with your engineering judgment.
Interviewers are in fact watching your AI interaction the whole time; this assumption is wrong.
Right — what's actually scored is whether you're still breaking down the problem and checking results; the prompt is just the tool.

q: AI 编码面试中四个稳定评估维度是什么？（多选）
q_en: What are the four stable evaluation areas in AI coding interviews? (Select all that apply.)
options: 问题解决和方法
对 AI 的控制
验证习惯
沟通
options_en: Problem-solving and approach.
Control over the AI.
Verification habits.
Communication.
why: 不同公司具体形式不同，但这四项在候选人和面试官访谈中被反复描述为一致的评分核心。
why_en: Regardless of company format, these four areas stay consistent as the core evaluation criteria.
diagram:
flowchart TD
  Eval[Evaluation] --> Solve[Problem solving]
  Eval --> Control[AI control]
  Eval --> Verify[Verification]
  Eval --> Communicate[Communication]

rows: 能否拆解并排出优先级
是你在指挥还是它在指挥
是否复查测试还是照单全收
过程是否让面试官跟上

optionExplanations: 看你能不能把问题拆对顺序，不是靠 AI 硬撞出答案。
看架构和实现的关键决定是你在做，还是被 AI 牵着走。
看你是照单全收 AI 的输出，还是会跑测试挑边界情况。
看面试官能不能全程跟上你的判断，而不是只看到最后的代码。
optionExplanations_en: Checks whether you break the problem down in the right order instead of letting AI brute-force it.
Checks whether you, not the AI, are making the key architecture and implementation calls.
Checks whether you actually test and review AI's output instead of accepting it as-is.
Checks whether the interviewer can follow your judgment throughout, not just see the final code.
scenario: 你只剩两周准备 AI 编码面试，必须挑真正进评分表的几项来练，不能平均用力。
scenario_en: You have two weeks to prep and must train only the areas that actually land on the scorecard.

q: 把四个核心能力按工作流大致排好：
q_en: Put the four core skills into a rough workflow order:
steps: 验证 AI 给出的代码
why: 工作流通常是先有方法，再驱动 AI，再验证，沟通贯穿全程；沟通也可以从一开始就并行进行。
why_en: The workflow starts with approach, then AI control and verification, with communication running throughout.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Orient[Orient] --> Plan[Plan]
  Plan --> Drive[Drive AI]
  Drive --> Verify[Verify]
  Verify --> Communicate[Explain]

scenario: 面试刚开始，题目和代码库都还没理解清楚，但 AI 聊天框已经打开。
scenario_en: The interview has just started; you do not yet understand the task or codebase, but the AI chat box is already open.
q: 强候选人的第一反应是什么？
q_en: What should a strong candidate do first?
options: 让 AI 决定架构
跳过沟通，先闷头做
立即把原始题目粘给 AI
先读题和代码，形成方案，再提示 AI
options_en: Let the AI decide the architecture.
Skip communication and just start working silently.
Immediately paste the raw problem into the AI.
Read the problem and code first, form a plan, then prompt the AI.
why: 问题解决能力仍是基本盘，AI 只会放大你有没有先想清楚；没有方案时提示 AI，只是让它替你猜。
why_en: Strong candidates understand the problem and form an approach before prompting the AI, because AI only amplifies whether you already have a plan.
whenOtherWins: 如果题目是明确的一行 bug，也要先花几十秒定位相关路径，而不是完全跳过理解。
tradeoff: 先理解需求再提示 AI vs 直接把原题丢给 AI 自由发挥
optionExplanations: 架构判断应该你来做；把它交给 AI，等于让工具替你决定方向。
沉默省不了时间，反而让面试官看不到你在想什么。
题目还没读懂就丢给 AI，它只能照着不完整的理解瞎猜一个方案。
对，先花几分钟摸清需求和代码结构，再提示 AI，才是让 AI 执行你的判断而不是替你猜。
optionExplanations_en: Architecture calls should be yours; handing that to the AI just lets the tool pick the direction for you.
Staying silent doesn't save time, it just leaves the interviewer with nothing to follow.
Pasting the problem before you understand it forces the AI to guess from an incomplete read.
Right — spending a few minutes on the requirements and code first means the AI executes your judgment instead of guessing for you.

q: 问题解决阶段常见错误有哪些？（多选）
q_en: What are common mistakes during the problem-solving phase? (Select all that apply.)
options: 先读题并口头说明计划
没有自己的计划就把原题粘给 AI
跟随 AI 做本该由你决定的架构选择
AI 卡住时追随它提出的大重写建议
options_en: Reading the problem first and stating your plan out loud.
Pasting the raw problem into AI without forming your own plan first.
Following the AI into architectural decisions that should be yours to make.
Chasing an AI-suggested big rewrite when the model is stuck and just guessing.
why: 这三个错误都说明候选人把方向权交给了 AI，而不是用 AI 执行自己的判断。
why_en: These mistakes all show the candidate handing direction to the AI instead of using it to execute their own judgment.
optionExplanations: 这恰恰是该做的动作，不是错误——读题加说计划才是正确开场。
没想清楚就转发原题，等于让 AI 替你把整个问题理解一遍，你没法纠偏。
架构该你拍板，跟着 AI 走等于把工程判断权让出去。
卡住时的大重写建议往往只是模型在猜，追下去只会吃光剩余时间。
optionExplanations_en: This is actually the right opening move, not a mistake — read first, then state your plan.
Forwarding the raw problem before you understand it means the AI builds on your incomplete read, and you can't correct it later.
Architecture calls should be yours; following the AI here hands over your engineering judgment.
A stuck AI's big-rewrite suggestion is usually just a guess, and chasing it burns your remaining time.
scenario: 45 分钟的 AI 编码面试刚开始，题目是在陌生仓库里加一个搜索功能。
scenario_en: A 45-minute AI coding interview just started: add a search feature inside an unfamiliar codebase.

scenario: 你花了两分钟读需求和代码，还没对面试官说过一句话，AI 聊天框在等你输入。
scenario_en: You have spent two minutes reading the requirements and code without saying anything to the interviewer, and the AI chat box is waiting.
q: 接下来应该如何向面试官表达？
q_en: What should you say to the interviewer next?
options: "这个问题我打算全部交给 AI 去处理。"
什么都不说，一直沉默地自己往下读
"这段代码我不打算读，直接开始就行。"
"我先花几分钟确认需求和代码结构，再开始提示 AI。"
options_en: "I'm going to hand this whole problem over to the AI."
Say nothing at all and just keep reading in silence.
"I'm not going to read this code, I'll just start right away."
"I'm going to take a couple of minutes to confirm the requirements and code structure before I prompt the AI."
why: 简短说明能把取向步骤变成可见的专业流程，而不是让面试官觉得你在停滞或走神。
why_en: Briefly narrating your orientation step makes it visible and intentional instead of looking like silent stalling.
whenOtherWins: 如果面试官已经给出非常具体的入口点，可以直接说明你会先检查那条路径，省去通读全部代码。
tradeoff: 开口说明取向过程 vs 默不作声直接埋头进行
optionExplanations: 这句话把责任全推给了 AI，面试官还是不知道你此刻在做什么。
两分钟静默在面试官眼里很容易被读成卡壳，不是专注。
跳过阅读代码是被反复点名的错误，这句话等于提前告诉面试官你没做审阅。
对，这句话把你的取向动作变成看得见的专业步骤，面试官能跟上。
optionExplanations_en: This line hands everything to the AI and still leaves the interviewer guessing what you're doing.
Two minutes of silence easily reads as being stuck, not focused, to the interviewer.
Skipping the code read is a well-known mistake; saying it out loud just confirms you didn't review.
Right — saying this out loud turns quiet reading time into a visible, professional move the interviewer can follow.

q: 多位面试官对 AI 使用的核心期待是什么？
q_en: What is the core expectation interviewers have for AI use?
options: 由 AI 替候选人决定整体架构方向
候选人全程只做复制粘贴的动作
候选人在面试全程完全不用 AI
AI 不拍板，由候选人决策、AI 负责执行
options_en: The AI decides the overall architecture direction for the candidate.
The candidate does nothing but copy and paste the whole time.
The candidate doesn't use AI at all for the entire interview.
The AI doesn't call the shots; the candidate decides and the AI executes.
why: 候选人要坐在驾驶位，AI 是执行快但偶尔出错的搭档，一旦 AI 开始做架构判断，评估的核心信号就消失了。
why_en: Interviewers expect the candidate to make the decisions and use AI only to execute them.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Candidate[Candidate] --> Direction[Sets direction]
  Direction --> AI[AI writes]
  AI --> Review[Candidate reviews]
  Review --> Code[Accepted code]
optionExplanations: 这正是面试官反复强调要避免的情形，不是期待。
候选人角色不该被压缩成复制粘贴，判断力才是评估重点。
这类面试默认你会用 AI，完全不用反而不是期待。
对，候选人拍板决策、AI 负责执行，这才是驾驶位关系。
optionExplanations_en: This is exactly what interviewers say to avoid, not what they expect.
The candidate's role shouldn't shrink to copy-paste; judgment is what's being evaluated.
These interviews assume you'll use AI; avoiding it entirely isn't the expectation.
Right — you make the calls, the AI just carries them out; that's the driver's-seat relationship.
scenario: 面试官全程只观察你和 AI 的协作过程，并据此判断你的工程判断力。
scenario_en: The interviewer only watches how you and the AI work together, and judges your engineering judgment from that.

scenario: 一位 Rippling 候选人给出的初始方案是正确的。
scenario_en: A Rippling candidate gives a correct initial approach.
q: 这位候选人仍然可能因为什么得到负面反馈？
q_en: Why might this candidate still receive negative feedback?
options: 题目太简单
手写了太多注释
过度依赖 AI 做后续实现决策
没有使用任何编辑器
options_en: The problem was too easy.
They wrote too many hand-written comments.
They relied too heavily on AI for later implementation decisions.
They didn't use an editor at all.
why: 知道要做什么还不够；如果后续实现选择都交给 AI，面试官依然看不到你在负责地做决定。
why_en: Even with a correct initial approach, relying too heavily on AI for implementation decisions can still hurt the signal.
optionExplanations: 反馈和题目难度没有关系，方向对不代表就没问题。
注释多少不是这条反馈指向的问题。
对，初始方向对了，但后续实现细节都让 AI 拍板，面试官照样看不到你的判断。
工具选择跟这条反馈无关，问题出在谁在做决定。
optionExplanations_en: The feedback had nothing to do with difficulty; a correct direction doesn't guarantee a clean signal.
Comment count isn't what this feedback is about.
Right — the initial direction was fine, but letting AI own every later build decision still hides your judgment.
Tooling choice has nothing to do with this feedback; the issue is who's making the decisions.

scenario: Canva 式面试中，AI 每生成一段代码后，面试官都会问"这段代码做什么？"
scenario_en: In a Canva-style interview, after each AI-generated code block, the interviewer asks, "What does this code do?"
q: 这个问题主要评估什么？
q_en: What is this question mainly evaluating?
options: 你是否能隐藏错误
你是否背下所有语法
你是否能让 AI 更快输出
你是否理解并掌控生成逻辑
options_en: Whether you can hide mistakes.
Whether you have memorized all the syntax.
Whether you can make the AI produce output faster.
Whether you understand and are in control of the generated logic.
why: 如果你答不上来 AI 代码在做什么，说明你可能只是接受了输出，而没有真正审阅和拥有它。
why_en: Being asked what the code does tests whether you understand and own the generated logic, not whether you memorized syntax.
whenOtherWins: 如果单次输出很长，可以先说明你会逐块阅读，再解释关键路径和你还不确定的地方。
tradeoff: 能讲清生成逻辑并主动审阅 vs 全盘接受AI输出不追问
optionExplanations: 这个问题给不了你任何藏拙的空间，答不上来只会更暴露没审阅。
生成代码考的不是语法记忆，这条追问和背诵没关系。
生成速度快慢不是面试官在追的东西，这条追问跟速度无关。
对，答不出这段代码在做什么，说明你只是接受了输出，没真正审过。
optionExplanations_en: This question gives you nowhere to hide; not answering it just exposes that you never reviewed.
Generated code doesn't test syntax recall; this follow-up has nothing to do with memorization.
Output speed isn't what the interviewer is probing for here.
Right — going blank here usually means you accepted the output without really owning its logic.

q: 对 AI 控制不足的常见错误有哪些？（多选）
q_en: What are common signs of weak control over the AI? (Select all that apply.)
options: 未评估就接受 AI 的架构建议
把 AI 输出当成完成品而不是草稿
AI 偏离原计划时不重定向
每次输出后都检查是否符合预期
options_en: Accepting AI's architectural suggestions without evaluating them.
Treating AI output as a finished product instead of a draft to review.
Not redirecting the AI when it drifts away from the original plan.
Checking whether each output matches expectations after it comes back.
why: 这三个行为都让 AI 从执行者变成了决策者，削弱了候选人本该展示的工程判断信号。
why_en: These behaviors let the AI become the decision-maker instead of the executor, weakening the candidate's engineering-judgment signal.
optionExplanations: 没评估就照单全收，等于把架构决定权拱手让给 AI。
把草稿当终稿会跳过复核，边界错误留到最后才炸出来。
看到 AI 跑偏却不纠正，面试官会以为是 AI 在主导，不是你。
这恰恰是该做的事，不是错误——持续核对才能早发现偏差。
optionExplanations_en: Accepting it without evaluating hands the architecture call straight over to the AI.
Treating a draft as final skips review, so edge-case bugs only surface at the very end.
Watching the AI drift without redirecting it makes the interviewer think the AI is driving, not you.
This is actually the right habit, not a mistake — checking every output catches drift early.
scenario: 面试进行到一半，AI 给出的实现开始偏离你开场定下的分层方案。
scenario_en: Halfway through the interview, the AI's implementation starts drifting from the layered design you set at the start.

q: 补全 AI 角色类比：
q_en: Complete the analogy for AI's role:
text: 可以把 AI 当作一个非常{{快速}}、但偶尔{{错误}}的结对伙伴；你是负责方向的{{工程师}}。
why: 这个类比能帮助你保持审阅和决策责任，而不是被输出速度迷惑。
why_en: Treat AI as a very fast but occasionally wrong pair partner while you remain the responsible engineer.

q: 为什么验证习惯在 AI 编码面试中格外重要？
q_en: Why are verification habits especially important in AI coding interviews?
options: AI 生成的输出永远无法直接运行起来
验证这个动作只有初级工程师才需要做
面试官全程都不会去看你的测试结果
AI 会引入错误假设、漏边界和看似正确的 bug
options_en: AI-generated output can never actually be run at all.
Verification is something only junior engineers need to bother with.
The interviewer never looks at your test results at all.
AI can introduce wrong assumptions, missed edge cases, and bugs that look correct.
why: AI 生成代码速度快，也会同样快速地生成隐蔽错误；主动审阅和测试是在向面试官展示你对正确性负责。
why_en: Verification matters because AI can quickly produce plausible-looking code with wrong assumptions or missed edge cases.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  AIOutput[AI output] --> Unknown[Could be wrong]
  Unknown --> Tests[Run tests]
  Unknown --> Types[Check types]
  Tests --> Confidence[Confidence]
  Types --> Confidence
optionExplanations: AI 代码通常是能跑的，问题在于结果对不对，不是能不能运行。
验证是所有候选人都要展示的习惯，不分资历。
测试正是验证习惯里的关键动作，面试官恰恰在看这个。
对，AI 出错的方式往往是隐蔽的：假设错了、边界漏了、代码看着还挺像对的。
optionExplanations_en: AI code usually runs fine; the issue is whether the result is correct, not whether it runs.
Verification is a habit every candidate is expected to show, regardless of seniority.
Tests are exactly the key move inside verification habits — that's what interviewers watch for.
Right — AI's mistakes tend to be quiet ones: a bad assumption baked in, an edge case skipped, code that just looks right.
scenario: AI 十秒生成了 80 行改动，你只剩 30 分钟，而这段代码要处理分页边界。
scenario_en: The AI wrote 80 lines in ten seconds; you have 30 minutes left and this code has to handle pagination edge cases.

q: 验证习惯差的常见表现有哪些？（多选）
q_en: What are common signs of poor verification habits? (Select all that apply.)
options: 每次生成后不运行代码，最后才发现级联失败
AI 输出看起来对就跳过阅读
因为时间紧就跳过测试
每个有意义改动后都运行测试
options_en: Not running the code after each generation, only discovering cascading failures at the end.
Skipping the read-through because the AI output looks right at a glance.
Skipping tests because time is tight.
Running tests after every meaningful change.
why: 这些行为会让错误一路堆积到面试后期，修复时间往往远大于早期验证本该花的成本。
why_en: Poor verification lets errors pile up until they are far more expensive to fix than if they had been caught early.
optionExplanations: 错误攒到最后一起爆发，定位单个问题反而要花更久。
看起来对不代表真的对，边界错误最容易藏在这种自信里。
省下的测试时间，几乎总要在后面用双倍时间还回去。
这才是该做的动作——改动还小的时候发现问题，修复成本最低。
optionExplanations_en: Stacking up problems instead of catching them means isolating any single cause later takes far longer.
Looking right doesn't mean being right — edge-case bugs hide exactly behind that confidence.
Time saved by skipping tests almost always gets paid back double later.
This is the right move — catching issues while the change is still small keeps the fix cheap.
scenario: 面试只剩 10 分钟，你前面连续接受了五次 AI 生成，一次测试都没跑过。
scenario_en: Ten minutes are left and you've accepted five AI generations in a row without running the tests once.

q: AI 编码面试中的沟通核心动作是什么？
q_en: What is the core communication move in an AI coding interview?
options: 只在整场面试快结束时才做一次总结
把所有解释责任都完全交给 AI
为了不打断面试官就一直保持沉默
提示前说意图，输出后说结果，偏离时指出问题
options_en: Only give one summary right near the end of the whole interview.
Hand all explaining responsibility completely over to the AI.
Stay completely silent the whole time to avoid interrupting the interviewer.
State your intent before prompting, narrate the result after, and flag it when things drift.
why: 沟通要让面试官看到你的过程控制，而不只是屏幕上出现的代码，这需要在提示前后都开口。
why_en: Communication makes your process control visible before, during, and after each AI prompt, not just at the end.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Intent[State intent] --> Prompt[Prompt AI]
  Prompt --> Review[Review aloud]
  Review --> Result[Share result]
  Result --> Next[Next move]
optionExplanations: 面试官需要全程跟上你，不能等到最后才补一句总结。
AI 不会替你向面试官解释你的判断，这份责任跑不掉。
长时间沉默正是被反复点名的错误，不是礼貌。
对，提示前说意图、输出后说结果、偏离时喊停，这三拍才是沟通的核心节奏。
optionExplanations_en: The interviewer needs to follow along the whole time, not just get a summary at the end.
The AI won't explain your judgment to the interviewer for you — that responsibility stays yours.
Long silence is a repeatedly named mistake, not politeness.
Right — state intent before prompting, narrate the result after, and flag it when things drift; that three-beat rhythm is the core move.
scenario: 面试官只能靠你说出口的话评估判断力，屏幕上突然长出的几十行代码不会自己解释。
scenario_en: The interviewer can only judge you from what you say out loud; dozens of lines appearing on screen don't explain themselves.

q: 沟通阶段常见错误有哪些？（多选）
q_en: What are common communication mistakes? (Select all that apply.)
options: 长时间安静提示 AI
事后才解释刚刚做了什么
没有说明是否认同 AI 建议的 DFS pivot 就照做
提示前先说明下一步意图
options_en: Staying quiet for long stretches while prompting the AI.
Explaining what you just did only after the fact.
Following AI's suggested DFS pivot without saying whether you actually agreed with it.
Stating your next-step intent before you prompt.
why: 这些错误让面试官看不到你的实时判断，甚至会把一次合理的转向误解成被 AI 牵着走。
why_en: These communication mistakes hide your real-time judgment from the interviewer, or make a reasonable pivot look like the AI leading you.

termDefinitions.meaning: 深度优先搜索，一种沿着一条路径尽量往深处走、走不通再回退的图/树遍历算法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DFS is a graph or tree traversal algorithm that goes as deep as possible along one path before backtracking.

optionExplanations: 这段时间面试官完全没有东西可以评估，判断力等于隐身了。
叙述全推到动作之后，面试官只看到结果，看不到你当时怎么想的。
对 AI 提出的 DFS 转向不表态就照做，面试官分不清是你判断还是被带偏。
这正是该做的动作——提前说明意图，面试官能提前校准预期。
optionExplanations_en: There's nothing for the person grading you to evaluate during that stretch — your judgment goes invisible.
Pushing all narration to after the fact means whoever's grading you only sees the result, not your reasoning at the time.
Going along with the AI's DFS pivot without stating a position leaves people unsure whether it was your call or the model steering.
This is the right move — stating intent ahead of time lets whoever's watching calibrate before you even start.
scenario: 面试官在旁观屏幕，需要实时分辨哪些转向是你的决定、哪些是 AI 带的。
scenario_en: The interviewer is watching your screen and needs to tell in real time which pivots were your call and which came from the AI.

scenario: 你本周就要面试，准备时间只剩几个晚上。
scenario_en: Your interview is this week, and you only have a few evenings left to prepare.
q: 时间这么紧，最低限度该怎么安排准备？
q_en: With time this tight, what is the minimum useful prep plan?
options: 只把面试公司的名字背下来
只刷传统 Easy 难度算法题
完整看完所有学习内容但不做练习
读四维度、浏览两种形式，做一次完整练习
options_en: Only memorize the names of the interviewing companies.
Only grind traditional easy-difficulty algorithm problems.
Read through everything but never actually practice.
Read the four areas, skim the two formats, and do one full practice run.
why: 时间少时，先掌握评分标准和格式差异，再用一次实战练习，让双线沟通在真正面试前就不陌生。
why_en: With limited time, read the evaluation areas, skim the formats, and do one full practice run so the two-conversation juggle isn't new on the day.
whenOtherWins: 如果时间更多，应按 fundamentals 顺序系统练习，直到驱动 AI 变得自然。
tradeoff: 少而精：评分标准+格式+一次实战 vs 面面俱到但完全不练习
optionExplanations: 公司名单不会告诉你面试官到底在评什么。
这类面试的重点已经从算法背诵挪走了，刷 Easy 题练不出双线沟通的手感。
只读不练容易变成被动吸收，双线沟通到现场还是陌生的。
对，时间紧就把精力押在评分标准、格式差异和一次实战上，性价比最高。
optionExplanations_en: A company list tells you nothing about what's actually being scored.
The focus here has shifted away from algorithm memorization; easy drills won't build the feel for juggling two conversations.
Reading without practicing tends to stay passive; juggling two conversations at once is still unfamiliar on the day.
Right — when the clock is tight, spend it on the scoring criteria, format differences, and one hands-on run-through.

scenario: 你有较多准备时间，而且知道自己审阅 AI 输出的习惯不够稳。
scenario_en: You have more prep time, and you know your habit of reviewing AI output is not steady enough.
q: 更合理的学习方式是什么？
q_en: What is the better study plan?
options: 只把公司列表背下来就当准备好了
干脆跳过验证相关的那部分学习内容
只读一遍 overview 概览，完全不做练习
按 fundamentals 顺序学习，针对弱点维度加练
options_en: Just memorize the company list and call yourself ready.
Just skip the verification-related material entirely.
Only read through the overview once, with zero practice.
Work through the fundamentals in order, adding practice on your weak area.
why: Fundamentals 直接映射四个评估维度，时间充足时按顺序学习，再针对验证这个弱项加练，能补齐工作流。
why_en: The fundamentals map directly to the evaluation areas, so with more time, work through them in order and add extra practice on your weak spot.
whenOtherWins: 如果弱项已经非常明确，也可以直接跳到对应技能模块先补，而不必按顺序从头学。
tradeoff: 按顺序系统学习+补弱项 vs 只读概览不针对性练习
optionExplanations: 公司列表提升不了你审阅 AI 输出的能力。
跳过验证正好回避了你自己承认的弱项，面试当天这个短板还在。
浅读一遍不会针对性补强弱项，时间再多也没用在刀刃上。
对，系统学完整个工作流，再专门给验证这个弱项加练，才是把时间用在刀刃上。
optionExplanations_en: A company list won't improve your ability to review AI output.
Skipping verification avoids exactly the weak spot you already admitted to; it's still there on interview day.
A shallow read doesn't target the one area you're behind on, so extra time goes to waste.
Right — go through the material top to bottom, then add focused practice on verification, and the time actually counts.

q: 哪些 fundamentals 和评估维度的对应关系正确？（多选）
q_en: Which fundamentals-to-evaluation mappings are correct? (Select all that apply.)
options: Codebase orientation 和 Planning 覆盖 approach
Driving the AI 覆盖 control
Verification and testing 覆盖 verification
Communication 覆盖 narration
options_en: Codebase orientation and planning cover the approach dimension.
Driving the AI covers the control dimension.
Verification and testing covers the verification dimension.
Communication covers the narration piece.
why: Fundamentals 明确映射到四大评分维度，方便按弱点跳转学习而不必从头通读。
why_en: The fundamentals map directly onto the four scoring dimensions, so you can jump straight to your weak spot instead of reading everything in order.
optionExplanations: 对，取向和规划两篇一起支撑你怎么拆解问题这条维度。
对，驱动 AI 这篇教你怎么让自己而不是模型来定方向。
对，验证与测试这篇教你怎么审出 AI 输出里的隐蔽错误。
对，沟通这篇教你怎么把判断过程说给面试官听。
optionExplanations_en: Right — orientation and planning together build the skill for breaking down the problem.
Right — driving the AI teaches you to keep direction in your own hands instead of the model's.
Right — verification and testing teaches you to catch AI's quiet mistakes.
Right — communication teaches you to narrate your judgment out loud for the interviewer.
scenario: 只剩几天准备时间，你想按自己最弱的那个评分维度直接跳到对应的 fundamentals 章节。
scenario_en: With only a few days left, you want to jump straight to the fundamentals chapter matching your weakest scoring dimension.

q: 只读不练，为什么很难在面试当天保持双线沟通的节奏？
q_en: Why is reading without practice not enough to keep the two-conversation rhythm on interview day?
options: 因为做练习就可以完全跳过前面的知识学习
因为只要练习过一次就一定能通过面试
因为练习唯一的作用就是背下题目的标准答案
阅读偏被动，动手才能练出双线沟通和 AI 控制的手感
options_en: Because doing practice lets you skip learning the material beforehand entirely.
Because practicing once is enough to guarantee you will pass.
Because the only thing practice does is help you memorize question answers.
Reading stays passive; only hands-on reps build the feel for the dual conversation and AI control.
why: AI 编码面试的节奏只有在动手时才会暴露，尤其是提示、验证和沟通之间的切换，光靠阅读很难在现场保持住。
why_en: The real rhythm of an AI coding interview only shows up when you actually practice, especially switching between prompting, verifying, and communicating.
optionExplanations: 练习和学习是互补关系，不是谁能替代谁。
练一次能提升熟练度，但不保证结果，题目本身也会变。
练习的价值不止背答案，题目每次都不一样，背答案没用。
对，阅读是被动吸收，只有真上手才能把双线切换和 AI 控制练成本能反应。
optionExplanations_en: Practice and learning complement each other; neither replaces the other.
One round builds familiarity, not a guarantee — and the problems themselves change each time.
Practice is worth more than memorizing an answer, since the problems change with every round anyway.
Right — reading is passive; only hands-on reps turn the dual-conversation switch and AI control into instinct.
scenario: 你已经读完全部 fundamentals 章节，但一次带 AI 的模拟面试都没做过。
scenario_en: You've read every fundamentals chapter but haven't done a single mock interview with an AI assistant.

scenario: 你做完一次 AI coding practice，反馈指出你让模型接管了方向。
scenario_en: After an AI coding practice round, the feedback says you let the model take over the direction.
q: 下一次练习前，哪段自我提示最能修正这个问题？
q_en: Before the next practice round, which self-prompt best fixes this problem?
options: 先让 AI 决定这次要用的完整架构方案
只追求让 AI 一次生成更多的代码行数
这次练习干脆完全跳过任何测试环节
每次提示前写下计划、AI 要执行的步骤、以及验证方式
options_en: Let the AI decide the full architecture for this round first.
Just chase having the AI generate more lines of code at once.
Skip any testing step entirely for this practice round.
Before each prompt, write down the plan, the AI's task, and how to verify it.
why: 把计划、执行请求和验证方式绑在一起写下来，能强迫你先做判断，再让 AI 执行，而不是反过来。
why_en: Writing down the plan, the AI's task, and the verification method before each prompt forces you to own the direction instead of following the AI's.
whenOtherWins: 如果主要弱点是沟通而不是控制，还要加上提示前口头说明和输出后复述的练习。
tradeoff: 先写计划/验证方式再提示 vs 直接提示后被动接受输出
codeSample:
Before each AI prompt:
1. My plan for this step is ...
2. I want the AI to implement ...
3. I will verify it by running ...
4. I will reject output that changes ...
optionExplanations: 这正是上次反馈点名的问题——把方向权提前让给了 AI，不是修正。
行数变多不代表你重新拿回了方向，量不是信号。
反馈说的是控制问题，跳过测试只会让同样的错误更难被发现。
对，把计划、执行请求、验证方式写在提示前，逼自己先判断再让 AI 执行，正对上反馈。
optionExplanations_en: This repeats exactly what the feedback flagged — handing direction to the AI early, not fixing it.
More lines doesn't mean you've regained control; volume isn't the signal here.
The feedback was about control, not testing — skipping tests just makes the same mistake harder to catch.
Right — spelling out your plan, what you want the AI to build, and how you'll check it before every prompt keeps you steering, which directly answers the feedback.

q: 把 AI 编码面试成功模型排好：
q_en: Put the AI coding interview success model in order:
steps: 让 AI 快速执行具体实现
why: 通过者不是不用 AI，而是在自己掌控方向时让 AI 打字，并持续验证结果。
why_en: Successful candidates understand the context, communicate a plan, use AI to implement, and verify the result.
diagram:
flowchart LR

scenario: 你让 AI 生成了一段代码，跑了一遍测试全绿，时间还够。
scenario_en: You had AI generate some code, ran the tests and they all pass, and you still have time.
q: 此时跳过逐行审阅、直接进下一阶段，会有什么后果？
q_en: What happens if you skip the review and move on now, even though tests pass?
options: 没有影响，代码只要能跑通测试就够了
照样留下坏印象——审阅本身是掌控力信号
只是白白浪费时间，测试已经证明代码正确
只在代码真的出错时才会被面试官扣分
options_en: No effect — passing the tests is all that matters.
It still leaves a bad impression — the review itself is a control signal.
It just wastes time, since the tests already prove the code is correct.
You only lose points if the code actually turns out to be buggy.
why: 面试官评的是你是否在掌控，而不只是代码能否运行；审阅既抓 bug，也向面试官证明你在负责，跳过它即便代码碰巧能跑也丢掉这个信号。
why_en: Reviewers grade whether you're in control, not just whether the code runs — skipping the read, even when it works, signals you're not really driving.

termDefinitions.meaning: 人工智能，这里指面试里帮你生成/修改代码的编程助手模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AI here means the coding-assistant model that generates or edits code during the interview.

optionExplanations: 测试通过不是唯一评分标准，面试官还在看你有没有真的掌控代码。
对，审阅不只是为了抓 bug，它本身就是在向面试官证明你在掌控这份工作。
审阅不是浪费——测试绿了不代表逻辑符合你的意图，也不代表信号到位。
扣分不只发生在有 bug 时；即使代码碰巧能跑，不审阅也会显得你在被 AI 牵着走。
optionExplanations_en: Passing tests isn't the only thing scored; the interviewer is also watching whether you truly own the code.
Right — reviewing isn't only about catching bugs; it's how you show the interviewer you're in control of the work.
The review isn't wasted — green tests don't prove the logic matches your intent or that the signal landed.
Points aren't lost only when there's a bug; skipping review even on working code makes you look led by the AI.

scenario: 你下周有一场 AI 编码面试，但不确定这轮是 structured（面试方给 CoderPad 和固定模型）还是 open-ended（自带编辑器和 AI 工具）。
scenario_en: You have an AI coding interview next week but aren't sure if it's structured (they provide CoderPad and fixed models) or open-ended (your own editor and AI tools).
q: 面对这个不确定性，最靠谱的准备动作是什么？
q_en: Given this uncertainty, what's the most reliable prep move?
options: 向 recruiter 确认本轮的实际形式和可用工具
默认按 open-ended 准备，自带编辑器和 AI 工具
照网上最新的攻略文章准备，格式变化不大
structured 和 open-ended 全套都各准备一遍
options_en: Ask the recruiter to confirm this round's actual format and available tools.
Assume it's open-ended and prep with your own editor and AI tools.
Just follow the latest online guides — the format doesn't change much.
Prepare a full setup for both structured and open-ended separately.
why: 两种形式决定你是否要自带编辑器和 AI 工具，而格式在不同面试周期间会变；与其猜，不如向 recruiter 确认当前轮次的真实设置。
why_en: The two formats decide whether you bring your own editor and AI tools, and the format shifts between cycles — so confirm the current setup with your recruiter instead of guessing.
whenOtherWins: 如果 recruiter 已在邮件里写清了平台和可用模型，就不必再问，直接照那份说明准备即可。
tradeoff: 向 recruiter 核实真实格式 vs 按旧攻略或默认假设自行准备

termDefinitions.meaning: 结构化形式：面试方提供一切——浏览器环境（如 CoderPad）、固定的一组 AI 模型、从修 bug 到加功能到扩展的题目。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A structured interview: they hand you everything — a browser environment like CoderPad, a fixed set of AI models, and a bug-to-feature-to-scale problem.

termDefinitions.meaning: 开放形式：全靠你自己——用自己的编辑器和 AI 工具，共享屏幕，从零搭或基于已有代码库。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An open-ended interview: it's all you — your own editor and AI tools, screen shared, building from scratch or from an existing codebase.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个在线协作编程环境，浏览器里写和跑代码，structured 面试常用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CoderPad is a browser-based collaborative coding environment used in structured interviews.

termDefinitions.meaning: 招聘对接人（HR），负责安排你这场面试，知道本轮的实际形式和平台。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The recruiter is the hiring contact who schedules your interview and knows the round's actual format.

optionExplanations: 对，格式在不同周期间会变，只有 recruiter 知道你这轮到底给什么环境和模型。
默认 open-ended 可能猜错——若真是 structured，你自带的工具根本用不上。
网上攻略大多是猜测且更新滞后，靠它决定环境风险太大。
两套全准备既费时又没解决核心问题：你仍不知道现场到底用哪套工具。
optionExplanations_en: Right — the format shifts between cycles, and only the recruiter knows what environment and models your round provides.
Assuming open-ended can be wrong — if it's actually structured, your own tools won't be usable.
Online guides are mostly guesswork and lag behind; betting your setup on them is too risky.
Prepping both is time-consuming and dodges the core issue: you still don't know which tools you'll actually get.
